content.title: Random Network Distillation as a Diversity Metric for Both Image and Text Generation
content.abstract: Generative models are increasingly able to produce remarkably high quality images and text.  The community has developed numerous evaluation metrics for comparing generative models.  However, these metrics do not effectively quantify data diversity.  We develop a new diversity metric that can readily be applied to data, both synthetic and natural, of any type.  Our method employs random network distillation, a technique introduced in reinforcement learning.  We validate and deploy this metric on both images and text.  We further explore diversity in few-shot image generation, a setting which was previously difficult to evaluate.

content.one-sentence_summary: We present a novel, dataset agnostic framework for comparing diversity of generated data.
